code_label: Quantum Monte Carlo offers quadratic error improvement
text_span: It has been shown that estimation error in the quantum-based Monte Carlo is proportional to O(N−1), where N is the number of computational steps, compared with O(N−1/2) in the classical one.
rationale: States the motivating performance claim for quantum Monte Carlo versus classical Monte Carlo.

code_label: High-dimensional finance creates qubit pressure
text_span: the required qubit number is proportional to the number of the random numbers Nran
rationale: Identifies the qubit-scaling issue in prior quantum Monte Carlo implementations.

code_label: Credit portfolio loss can require many random numbers
text_span: The number of obligors can be O(106) for large portfolios, and so is the required random number.
rationale: Highlights the concrete high-dimensional finance setting motivating qubit reduction.

code_label: Sequential PRNG use reduces memory needs
text_span: we sequentially generate pseudo-random bit strings on a quantum register and calculate the integrand into another register.
rationale: Summarizes the paper’s central methodological idea.

code_label: Quantum amplitude estimation preserves speedup
text_span: This procedure leads to the same estimation result as classical Monte Carlo, but with quadratic speedup.
rationale: Claims the proposed approach retains quantum speedup while changing the sampling strategy.

code_label: PCG chosen for space and depth advantages
text_span: We propose an example of PRNG which can be easily implemented on a quantum circuit. It is permuted congruential generator (PCG)
rationale: Specifies the PRNG selected for implementation.

code_label: PCG has memory and computational advantages
text_span: This is the combination of the linear congruential method and permutation of bit string and has advantages in the aspect of memory (that is, required qubit number) and computational load (that is, circuit depth)
rationale: Explains why PCG is preferred over alternatives.

code_label: Credit risk and simple integration are demonstration targets
text_span: The first one is credit risk measurement, which is mentioned above. ... The second one is the integration of a simple multi-variable function
rationale: States the two application domains used to demonstrate the method.

code_label: Trade-off between qubits and depth is central
text_span: reduction of qubits. Although we will explain the detail in the next section, we here describe the outline.
rationale: Introduces the main trade-off framing the method.

code_label: Classical Monte Carlo samples only part of all patterns
text_span: we do not consider all patterns of random number values in the classical Monte Carlo.
rationale: Contrasts classical sampling with exhaustive quantum superposition.

code_label: Sampled expectation differs from true expectation
text_span: We sample only a part of patterns of the random numbers and the integrand and take a simple arithmetic average of the sampled integrand values as an approximation for Etrue.
rationale: Defines the target quantity Esamp used by the proposed algorithm.

code_label: Two assumptions underlie the proposed algorithm
text_span: we here describe the outline. In short, it is classical Monte Carlo on a quantum computer.
rationale: Signals that the method depends on specific assumptions about the integrand and PRNG gates.

code_label: Integrand must be sequentially computable
text_span: We assume that it takes Nran random numbers as arguments and is sequentially computed in Nran steps
rationale: States the first key assumption required for the algorithm.

code_label: PRNG gates must support stepping and jumping
text_span: we can choose some PRNG which consumes nPRN bits ... and construct two types of quantum gate.
rationale: States the second key assumption required for the algorithm.

code_label: Superposition over sample indices is prepared with Hadamards
text_span: Prepare a register Rsamp with nsamp qubits and generate a superposition of |0⟩, |1⟩, ..., |Nsamp −1⟩ with equal amplitudes
rationale: Describes the first step of the proposed quantum flow.

code_label: JPRN initializes subsequence starting points
text_span: operate JPRN, then the (iNran + 1)-th element of the sequence is set to the register RPRN
rationale: Describes how each sample branch gets its PRNG starting point.

code_label: PRNG and integrand are iterated sequentially
text_span: Iterate 4 and 5 until the calculation of the integrand ends.
rationale: Captures the sequential generation-and-evaluation loop.

code_label: Amplitude encoding converts sampled values to probabilities
text_span: encode the integrand value into the amplitude of |1⟩ in Rph using controlled rotations.
rationale: Describes the final encoding step before amplitude estimation.

code_label: Previous quantum Monte Carlo uses one register per random number
text_span: a quantum register is allocated to represent a random number
rationale: Summarizes the prior approach used for comparison.

code_label: Uniform PRNs must be converted to target distributions
text_span: we have to convert uniform random numbers to random numbers obeying a desired distribution.
rationale: Notes a necessary transformation in the proposed approach.

code_label: Distribution of integrand values emerges through PRNG
text_span: the distribution of the integrand value is generated through the PRNG in the method of this paper.
rationale: Explains how the sampled-value distribution is represented in the proposed method.

code_label: Not all functions fit the sequential form
text_span: it is just an assumption, that is, not all functions can be written like this.
rationale: Explicitly states a limitation of the method’s applicability.

code_label: Credit portfolio loss fits the sequential form
text_span: The credit portfolio risk measurement, which we will consider later, corresponds to this case.
rationale: Connects the method’s assumptions to the later finance application.

code_label: Error decomposes into sampling and amplitude-estimation parts
text_span: There are two sources of error. One is the diﬀerence between Esamp and Etrue
rationale: Introduces the paper’s error analysis for the proposed method.

code_label: Sampling error scales as inverse square root of sample count
text_span: it is at most cσ fNran N−1/2samp = cσfNran 2−nsamp/2
rationale: Gives the statistical error scaling for the sampled expectation.

code_label: Amplitude-estimation error scales inversely with oracle calls
text_span: the error of amplitude estimation, which we write as ∆Est.
rationale: Identifies the second error source and its dependence on oracle calls.

code_label: Quantum method keeps quadratic speedup over classical Monte Carlo
text_span: This is actually quadratic speed up compared with the classical Monte Carlo.
rationale: States the main complexity advantage of the proposed method.

code_label: Classical Monte Carlo error scales as inverse square root of oracle calls
text_span: the error is ∆class ∼ cσfNran N−1/2orac
rationale: Provides the classical baseline for comparison.

code_label: Previous quantum method estimates the true expectation directly
text_span: This method estimates Etrue itself
rationale: Describes the target of the earlier quantum approach used for comparison.

code_label: Self-updating modular multiplication is needed to avoid extra qubits

code_label: Random rotation uses controlled swaps on selected bits
text_span: Random rotation is easily implemented in a quantum circuit using controlled swap gate (Fredkin gate).

code_label: Xorshift is implemented with CNOT gates

code_label: Multiplication dominates PCG qubit and depth costs
text_span: dominant contribution comes from a multiplication and is O(n) and O(n2) respectively.
rationale: Summarizes the resource cost of the PRNG circuit.

code_label: Simulation result matches the sampled average

code_label: Qubit reduction increases circuit depth
text_span: It is clear that qubit number reduction proposed in this paper increases circuit depth.
rationale: States the principal trade-off and practical limitation of the approach.

code_label: Deep circuits may be impractical without error correction
text_span: Without quantum error correction [32–34], which is expected not to be realized in near-term quantum computer, such a deep circuit will not be performable.
rationale: Explicitly notes a feasibility constraint.

code_label: Partial parallelism is proposed when qubits are limited
text_span: we can parallelly generate Nran/n PRN sequences with n elements, calculate a part of the integrand using the elements in each sequence one-by-one
rationale: Describes a fallback strategy under limited qubit availability.
